今天的主题：科技、交通和道路安全。这组词在阅读的科技类文章、G 类 Section 1 和 2 的交通安全通知，口语 Part 1 的 Transport、Technology 话题，以及写作 Task 2 讨论「新科技利弊」时都很好用。

例句

  • Driverless cars are still a controversial technology in many countries.（无人驾驶汽车在很多国家仍是一项有争议的技术。）
  • Drivers must stop and let pedestrians proceed at a zebra crossing.（在斑马线前，司机必须停车让行人先走。）
  • Bright lights make cyclists more visible at night and help prevent accidents.（亮灯能让骑车人在夜里更显眼，有助于防止事故。）
  • The new app will alert users to any potential problems on the road.（这个新应用会提醒用户路上任何潜在的问题。）
  • Crossing the road outside a crossing is illegal in some countries.（在一些国家，不走人行横道过马路是违法的。）

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，再挑 5 个自己造句（试试用 controversial、potential、suitable 说说你对无人驾驶汽车的看法）。

BBC 6 Minute English：Sharing the road with driverless cars（和无人驾驶汽车共用马路）。这集讲没有司机的车怎么跟行人、跑步的人和骑车人「沟通」：格拉斯哥大学的 Stephen Brewster 教授测试了动画显示和彩色灯环两种信号，韩国的研究员 Ammar Al-Taie 讲了文化差异，比如韩国乱穿马路违法、英国人却常这么干。这集句子短、词汇贴近日常交通，比前两集好懂，适合用来练精听。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍，听不太懂可以先读懂原文再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，只听大意，回答开头的问题：第一个让完全无人驾驶的机器人出租车上街的城市是哪个？a) Philadelphia b) Phoenix c) San Francisco。顺便听出：Brewster 教授测试了哪两种信号？
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。Stephen Brewster 和 Ammar Al-Taie 两段采访是真实录音，语速稍快，多听几遍。
  4. 第三遍挑 Phil 讲过马路那段（"On my walk to work, I need to cross the road..."）跟读，模仿语调和连读。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：eye contact（眼神交流）、wave（挥手）、alert（提醒，警告）、animation（动画显示）、glance（扫一眼）、jaywalking（乱穿马路）。
点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）
💡 点击或悬停虚线词看中文；点击说话人名字可单独切换该段翻译

Phil：Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Phil.

Phil：大家好，这里是 BBC 学习英语的《六分钟英语》。我是菲尔。

Pippa：And I'm Pippa.

Pippa：我是皮帕。

Phil：Here at 6 Minute English, we love discussing new tech. One of the most controversial有争议的 technologies of recent years is driverless cars无人驾驶汽车, also known as self-driving cars自动驾驶汽车, autonomous自主的，自动的 cars or robotaxis机器人出租车.

Phil：在《六分钟英语》，我们很喜欢聊新科技。近几年最有争议的技术之一就是无人驾驶汽车，也叫自动驾驶汽车、自主汽车或者机器人出租车。

Pippa：Many people say they wouldn't feel safe in a car without a human driver, but there are concerns from other road users道路使用者 too – pedestrians行人, runners and cyclists骑自行车的人. How will driverless cars无人驾驶汽车 interact互动 with them? It's a problem Professor Stephen Brewster, from Glasgow University, has been working on. He explained more to BBC World Service programme Tech Life.

Pippa：很多人说坐在没有人类司机的车里会觉得不安全，但其他道路使用者也有顾虑，比如行人、跑步的人和骑自行车的人。无人驾驶汽车要怎么和他们互动呢？格拉斯哥大学的斯蒂芬·布鲁斯特教授一直在研究这个问题。他在 BBC 国际频道的节目《科技生活》里做了更多解释。

Stephen Brewster：If you're outside a vehicle right now, you can see the driver inside the vehicle, you can wave to them, they can see you, you can make eye contact眼神交流. But when you come to an autonomous自主的，自动的 vehicle, there's no person in the driving seat驾驶座, so how do you negotiate协商，商量 whether they're going to go, whether they're going to let you go?

Stephen Brewster：现在如果你在车外，你能看到车里的司机，可以向他挥手，他也能看到你，你们可以有眼神交流。但换成自动驾驶汽车，驾驶座上没有人，那你要怎么去协商：它是要先走，还是要让你先走？

Phil：On my walk to work, I need to cross the road. Usually, a driver makes eye contact眼神交流 with me. They look directly into my eyes and then wave me across. To wave means to raise your hand and move it from side to side左右来回. It's a gesture手势 for saying hello, or a way of telling a person to do something.

Phil：我走路上班时要过一条马路。通常司机会和我有眼神交流，他们直视我的眼睛，然后挥手让我过去。wave 的意思是举起手左右摆动。这是打招呼的手势，也可以用来示意别人做某件事。

Pippa：Luckily, Phil, you usually arrive safely at work and as yet到目前为止 there are no driverless cars无人驾驶汽车 in London. But, Phil, how would you feel about crossing that road in front of a robotaxi机器人出租车?

Pippa：幸好，菲尔，你一般都能平安到公司，而且到目前为止伦敦还没有无人驾驶汽车。不过菲尔，要是在一辆机器人出租车前面过那条马路，你会是什么感觉？

Phil：Well, maybe a little bit nervous. I might wait for it to go and go behind it or something.

Phil：嗯，可能有点紧张吧。我也许会等它先开走，然后从它后面过去之类的。

Pippa：Mmm... yeah, I get that. I think maybe as we get more used to越来越习惯 these technologies, we'll get more used to越来越习惯 how to deal with them and when to cross. But in this episode, we investigate调查，研究 the tech helping driverless cars无人驾驶汽车 communicate on the roads. We'll learn some useful new words and phrases, and as usual you'll find all the vocabulary on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

Pippa：嗯，我能理解。我觉得等我们越来越习惯这些技术，也会越来越清楚该怎么应对它们、什么时候过马路。不过这一集我们要探究的是帮助无人驾驶汽车在路上进行沟通的技术。我们会学一些有用的新单词和短语，跟往常一样，所有词汇都可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到。

Phil：But first, I have a question for you, Pippa. As you mentioned, we don't have self-driving cars自动驾驶汽车 here in London yet. So, which was the first city to have fully driverless robotaxis机器人出租车 on the streets? Was it:
a) Philadelphia,
b) Phoenix, or
c) San Francisco?

Phil：不过先问你一个问题，皮帕。就像你说的，伦敦还没有自动驾驶汽车。那么，第一个让完全无人驾驶的机器人出租车上街的城市是哪个？是 a) 费城，b) 凤凰城，还是 c) 旧金山？

Pippa：I'm going to say
b) Phoenix because I think it's quite a car-friendly适合开车的 city.

Pippa：我选 b) 凤凰城，因为我觉得那是个挺适合开车的城市。

Phil：OK. Well, we will find out the answer, but at the end of the programme. Because accidents are often caused by not seeing the oncoming迎面而来的 danger, Professor Brewster wants to make driverless cars无人驾驶汽车 more visible显眼的，看得见的. He discussed his work with BBC Tech Life's presenter主持人 Chris Vallance.

Phil：好的。答案我们节目最后揭晓。因为事故常常是没看到迎面而来的危险造成的，所以布鲁斯特教授想让无人驾驶汽车更显眼。他和 BBC《科技生活》的主持人克里斯·瓦兰斯聊了他的研究。

Chris Vallance：What kind of signals worked in terms of在……方面 alerting提醒，警告 pedestrians行人 and runners and cyclists骑自行车的人 to the intentions意图 of the vehicle?

Chris Vallance：在提醒行人、跑步者和骑车人注意车辆意图这方面，哪种信号效果好？

Stephen Brewster：We tested two things. We tested animations动画显示 and fixed, coloured light rings灯环. The animations动画显示 – they work well for pedestrians行人, but when it came to runners and cyclists骑自行车的人, they have much less time to make their decisions, so if you do a quick glance一瞥，扫一眼 at a vehicle, you don't really see the animation动画显示.

Stephen Brewster：我们测试了两样东西：动画显示，和固定的彩色灯环。动画对行人效果不错，但对跑步者和骑车人来说，他们做决定的时间少得多，所以如果你只是快速瞥一眼车，其实看不清那个动画。

Pippa：It's important to alert提醒，警告 people to driverless cars无人驾驶汽车. To alert提醒，警告 somebody means to warn them about a potential潜在的 danger. Some cars do this with animations动画显示 – displays of moving images. For example, a green man walking to signal it's safe to cross.

Pippa：提醒人们注意无人驾驶汽车很重要。alert somebody 的意思是提醒某人注意潜在的危险。有些车用动画来做到这一点，也就是活动图像的显示。比如显示一个走路的绿色小人，表示可以安全过马路。

Phil：Animations动画显示 alert提醒，警告 pedestrians行人 but are not suitable合适的 for runners and cyclists骑自行车的人, who are travelling too fast to react. They only have time for a glance一瞥，扫一眼. A glance一瞥，扫一眼 at something means a quick look. So, instead Stephen's team used coloured light rings灯环, similar to traffic lights, to warn cyclists骑自行车的人 and runners.

Phil：动画能提醒行人，但不适合跑步者和骑车人，他们速度太快，来不及反应，只来得及瞥一眼。a glance at something 的意思是快速看一眼。所以斯蒂芬的团队改用了类似红绿灯的彩色灯环来提醒骑车人和跑步者。

Pippa：Culture is another problem. The meaning of body language肢体语言 can change. For example, hand waving can mean 'please proceed继续前进' in one culture, but 'thank you' in another.

Pippa：文化是另一个问题。肢体语言的含义会变。比如挥手在一种文化里可能是「请先走」，在另一种文化里却是「谢谢」。

Phil：Ammar Al-Taie is a researcher at the Advanced Institute of Science and Technology in South Korea. Here, Ammar tells BBC World Service's Tech Life why Korean culture is especially suited to self-driving cars自动驾驶汽车.

Phil：阿马尔·阿尔泰是韩国一所科学技术院的研究员。下面，阿马尔向 BBC 国际频道的《科技生活》讲述为什么韩国文化特别适合自动驾驶汽车。

Ammar Al-Taie：In South Korea, for example, jaywalking乱穿马路 is illegal违法的, whereas而，然而 in the UK, you know, we tend to jaywalk乱穿马路 a lot.

Ammar Al-Taie：比如在韩国，乱穿马路是违法的，而在英国，你知道的，我们经常乱穿马路。

Pippa：Jaywalking乱穿马路 is an American English word. It means crossing the road at a place where crossing is not allowed or without taking care. Unlike Britain, jaywalking乱穿马路 is rare in South Korea, making the country safer for autonomous自主的，自动的 cars.

Pippa：jaywalking 是美式英语词，意思是在不允许过马路的地方过马路，或者过马路时不注意安全。和英国不同，韩国很少有人乱穿马路，这让这个国家对自动驾驶汽车来说更安全。

Phil：We've heard a lot about making driverless cars无人驾驶汽车 safer, and with plans to introduce them to London later this year, we'll soon see how safe they really are.

Phil：我们听了很多关于让无人驾驶汽车更安全的内容，而且伦敦计划今年晚些时候引进它们，很快我们就能知道它们到底有多安全了。

Pippa：Now, isn't it time to reveal揭晓，透露 the answer to your question, Phil?

Pippa：好了，菲尔，是不是该揭晓你那道题的答案了？

Phil：I asked you which city was the first to have self-driving cars自动驾驶汽车 on the road, and you said it was Phoenix... and that is the correct answer. Phoenix, Arizona, was the first city in the world to have self-driving cars自动驾驶汽车 operating on public roads without a human safety driver安全员, and that was in 2017. Let's recap回顾 the vocabulary we've learned, starting with eye contact眼神交流 – looking directly into someone's eyes.

Phil：我问你哪个城市最先让自动驾驶汽车上路，你说是凤凰城……答对了。亚利桑那州的凤凰城是世界上第一个让没有人类安全员的自动驾驶汽车在公共道路上运行的城市，那是在 2017 年。我们来回顾一下学过的词汇，先从 eye contact 开始，意思是直视某人的眼睛。

Pippa：To wave at someone is a way of saying hi, by raising your hand and waving it from side to side左右来回.

Pippa：wave at someone 是打招呼的一种方式，举起手左右摆动。

Phil：If you alert提醒，警告 someone, you warn them of potential潜在的 danger.

Phil：alert someone 就是提醒某人注意潜在的危险。

Pippa：An animation动画显示 is a display made up of moving images.

Pippa：animation 是由活动图像组成的显示内容。

Phil：A glance一瞥，扫一眼 is a quick, brief look at something.

Phil：glance 是快速、短暂地看一眼。

Pippa：And finally, the American English term jaywalking乱穿马路 means crossing the road where you're not supposed to. Once again, our six minutes are up. If you'd like to hear more programmes about technology, you'll find plenty on our tech topic page, all on our website. And there you'll also find a quiz and worksheet练习题 for this episode. Visit bbclearningenglish.com. We'll see you again soon, but for now it's goodbye.

Pippa：最后，美式英语词 jaywalking 的意思是在不该过马路的地方过马路。我们的六分钟又到了。如果你想听更多关于科技的节目，我们网站的科技专题页上有很多。在那里还能找到这一集的小测验和练习题。请访问 bbclearningenglish.com。我们很快再见，现在先说再见啦。

Phil：Goodbye!

Phil：再见！

过关标准：不看原文能用中文说出这集讲了什么（无人驾驶汽车为什么难和行人沟通，动画和灯环哪种适合谁，文化差异带来什么问题），6 个表达都知道意思，Phil 那段能流利读下来。

小练习

  1. In a job interview, try to make ______ ______ with the interviewer.（眼神交流）
  2. She took a quick ______ at her watch and left.（一瞥）
  3. A loud alarm will ______ staff if there is a fire.（提醒，警告）
  4. The teacher used an ______ to show how the heart works.（动画）
  5. ______ is dangerous, so always use the crossing.（乱穿马路）
  6. Children should hold an adult's hand and look out for ______ traffic.（迎面而来的）
点开看答案

开头那题选 b，Phoenix（亚利桑那州凤凰城），2017 年起就有不带人类安全员的自动驾驶汽车上路，Pippa 答对了。Brewster 教授测试的是动画显示和固定的彩色灯环：动画适合行人，灯环更适合速度快的跑步者和骑车人。填空：1. eye contact 2. glance 3. alert 4. animation 5. Jaywalking 6. oncoming

今天的小思考（为口语 Part 1 做准备）：Would you feel safe in a driverless car? 用英语说两三句：Personally, I would / wouldn't feel safe because ... / I think driverless cars could be useful for ..., but ...
